question.:question/problem:
Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=2{x}^{2}+1$ at the point $(2,9).$

$x\,+$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}+1.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(2{x}^{2}+1\right)=4 x
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,9):$

$$
m=f'(2)=8
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{1}{8}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(9\right)&=- \frac{1}{8}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right) \\ x+8\cdot y&=74.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(x)=4x-{x}^{3}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(4x-{x}^{3}\right)=4 - 3 x^{2}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,3):$

$$
m=f'(1)=1
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=-1.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(3\right)&=-1\left(x-\left(1\right)\right) \\ x+1\cdot y&=4.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{8}{{x}^{2}}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{8}{{x}^{2}}\right)=- \frac{16}{x^{3}}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,2):$

$$
m=f'(2)=-2
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(2\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right) \\ x-2\cdot y&=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{1}{8}{x}^{6}-\frac{7}{4}{x}^{3}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{1}{8}{x}^{6}-\frac{7}{4}{x}^{3}\right)=\frac{3 x^{2} \left(x^{3} - 7\right)}{4}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,-6):$

$$
m=f'(2)=3
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{1}{3}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(-6\right)&=- \frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right) \\ x+3\cdot y&=-16.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(x)=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{x}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt[3]{x}\right)=\frac{1}{2 x^{\frac{2}{3}}}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(\frac{1}{8},\frac{3}{4}):$

$$
m=f'(\frac{1}{8})=2
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{1}{2}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)&=- \frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)\right) \\ 8x+16\cdot y&=13.\end{aligned}
$$
